comparison: Both evaluate the catalog expansion from 6 to 21 species positively. OpenEval finds comprehensive support across claims C1-C4, C57-C68 with specific documentation. Peer reviewers explicitly acknowledge and accept the expansion (C2-C4, C66-C68, C202-C203), with all three reviewers confirming the addition of 15 new species. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with no concerns raised.

Both strongly support the gene conversion implementation (C70-C87). OpenEval documents specific technical parameters for D. melanogaster and E. coli, noting the msprime upgrade. Peer reviewers explicitly recognize this as a key new feature allowing simulations closer to actual recombination processes. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with no technical concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C88-C92, C97) but divergent evaluations. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED despite noting C91 is speculative and C97 is in development. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly citing Reviewer 2's concern about insufficient detail and incomplete implementation, with details deferred to a forthcoming publication. This represents a substantive disagreement on evidence sufficiency.

Both support the quality control and peer review process (C38-C42, C99-C102). OpenEval emphasizes procedural details and bug-finding evidence. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the rigorous two-person QC process and code review practices. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, treating this as a strength of the work.

Perfect claim overlap (C155-C158, C165-C168) for Anopheles gambiae implementation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents specific parameters with citations and Figure 2B. Peer Reviewer 1 specifically praises the detailed discussion highlighting non-trivial steps and care underlying the resource. No concerns raised by either.

Perfect claim overlap (C169-C197) for cattle model implementation. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents parameters and explicitly notes acknowledged limitations (C187, C194, C196). Peer reviewers praise the detailed discussion and note the extreme inbreeding demographic model as a valuable showcase. Both treat transparent limitation discussion as a strength.

Partial overlap on parameter entanglement guidelines (C103-C110). OpenEval covers broader scope including five parameter categories and specific examples. Peer reviewers focus on practical utility of missing parameter mechanisms. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. Reviewer 3 notes this section is widely relevant beyond stdpopsim users.

Strong overlap (C135-C145) on Table 1 parameter recommendations. OpenEval describes specific guidance and observable consequences for each parameter type. Peer reviewers emphasize practical utility of missing parameter mechanisms. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, with reviewers treating this as particularly useful contribution.

Perfect claim overlap (C111-C133) on simulation limitations discussion. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes thorough, well-cited discussion of sampling, inference methods, and neutral evolution assumptions. Peer reviewers treat transparent limitation acknowledgment as a strength, with Reviewer 1 noting no technical or conceptual concerns.

Partial overlap on community-driven aspects (C62-C65). OpenEval includes these claims within broader catalog expansion evaluation (R1). Peer reviewers separately evaluate community engagement, with editor and reviewers acknowledging the community-curated nature and contribution to reproducibility. Both are SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates chromosome-scale simulation rationale (C43-C55) as SUPPORTED, citing coherent rationale with supporting citations for capturing gene organization, correlations, linked selection, and computational feasibility. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates guidance for incomplete assemblies (C146-C154) as SUPPORTED, noting clear practical guidance with explicit trade-offs and context-dependent recommendations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims.

OpenEval evaluates scientific context and motivation (C5-C26) as SUPPORTED, noting logical progression from data availability through applications to simulation requirements with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these introductory claims.

OpenEval evaluates summary and future directions (C198-C212) as SUPPORTED, noting well-documented accomplishments and clearly stated educational objectives. Minimal overlap with peer results (C202-C203 in R1, C206-C207 in R4), but no dedicated peer evaluation of the conclusion section.

OpenEval evaluates expansion motivation (C29-C30, C59-C61) as SUPPORTED, noting clear rationale for broader species coverage based on community feedback. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these motivational claims.

OpenEval rates speculative future claims (C91, C134, C195, C197, C209, C210, C213, C215) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are predictions rather than demonstrated results. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these speculative elements, though some overlap with R3 (C91) and R6 (C195, C197) where they are embedded in larger evaluations.
